## Overview

Rotating machinery fails through vibration: imbalance, misalignment, bearing stiffness and resonance at critical speeds. This project builds a real-time measurement and analysis chain for a marine rotor, with the aim of identifying its vibration modes. The chain acquires accelerometer signals on an OPAL-RT OP4512 real-time simulator, computes the spectrum live, and identifies natural frequencies and mode shapes with an impact-hammer test.

## Objectives

::: {.objectives}
- Acquire accelerometer signals in real time on an OPAL-RT OP4512 simulator.
- Compute the vibration spectrum live and compare it with an SR785 dynamic signal analyzer.
- Identify natural frequencies, damping and mode shapes with an impact-hammer test.
:::

## Measurement chain

Rotor dynamics is the study of vibration in rotating systems, including critical speeds, whirling and instabilities. Monitoring vibration in real time is the first line of defence against these problems.

::: {.steps}
::: {.step}
**1. Sense**<br>GY-61 (ADXL335) three-axis accelerometer
:::
::: {.step}
**2. Acquire**<br>OPAL-RT OP4512 reads and processes the signals in real time
:::
::: {.step}
**3. Analyse**<br>Live FFT on the simulator and on an SR785 dynamic signal analyzer
:::
::: {.step}
**4. Identify**<br>Impact-hammer test for natural frequencies, damping and modes
:::
:::

### Real-time vibration acquisition

The accelerometer signals are read by the simulator and shown live, so imbalance, misalignment and resonance appear as changes in the measured vibration while the rotor runs.

### Real-time FFT

An FFT is computed on each incoming frame of data, which turns the time signal into its frequency content as it arrives. In the demonstration the simulator adds frequency components to a sine input, and the SR785 analyzer shows the same spectrum.

```{=html}
<figure class="vid solo"><div class="vid-frame"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/vjWWo3XZ-ac" title="Real-time FFT Demonstration | Dynamic Signal Analyzer SR785 | Opal-RT 4512" loading="lazy" allow="accelerometer; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe></div><figcaption>Real-time FFT with the SR785 and OP4512 · <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vjWWo3XZ-ac">Watch on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
```

### Impact hammer test

Experimental modal analysis finds the natural frequencies, damping and mode shapes of a structure. An instrumented hammer excites the structure, and the accelerometer and the SR785 analyzer record the response. Knowing the natural frequencies shows which operating speeds to avoid.

```{=html}
<figure class="vid solo"><div class="vid-frame"><iframe src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/bheadOo6iWs" title="Real-time Impact Hammer Test Demonstration" loading="lazy" allow="accelerometer; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe></div><figcaption>Impact hammer test · <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bheadOo6iWs">Watch on YouTube</a></figcaption></figure>
```

## Background: real-time HIL experiment

The first hands-on experiment was a DC motor hardware-in-the-loop test, run to show why real-time systems matter. A LaunchXL-F280049C board driven from Simulink in external mode streams data over USB without true real-time execution, and samples are lost as the frequency rises. In a 5-second test the number of points received against those expected was:

<div class="bars">
<div class="bar-row"><span class="bar-label">1 Hz</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill" style="width:80%"></span></span><span class="bar-val">4 of 5 points</span></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="bar-label">2 Hz</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill" style="width:70%"></span></span><span class="bar-val">7 of 10 points</span></div>
<div class="bar-row"><span class="bar-label">10 Hz</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar-fill" style="width:42%"></span></span><span class="bar-val">21 of 50 points</span></div>
</div>

An NI PCIe-6361 DAQ in connected I/O mode recorded at higher rates but has no embedded-system features. The dSPACE MicroLabBox 1202 offers both, with high-speed acquisition and no data loss, and this experience led to the real-time work above.

